articles.title: My mother’s phone calls became stranger, but I couldn’t visit. A rescue dog helped me reach her
articles.summary: Conversation was difficult. But Sally, a dear old German shepherd, gave me a glimpse of my mother’s emotional state. My mother had been wanting a dog for years. She lived in Perth, on the other side of the country to her children and grandchildren who were all grown up.
body: What I didn’t know was that the forbidding fence he was building, the gate operated by keypad and code, wasn’t just to contain a dog. It was to contain my mother.

Dogs became scarce during the Covid pandemic. There wasn’t much on offer at the local pound. In the winter of 2020, my mother and stepfather drove for several hours to collect Sally from a rescue shelter in a distant town. She was a chunky, ageing German shepherd, perhaps 10 or 11, with dense black fur and a grey muzzle, hard of hearing and stiff in the hips. Sally had been let go from a farm as she could no longer jump into the back of the ute. My stepfather lifted her on to a picnic blanket on the backseat of the car and they drove her home.
A few days later I rang my mother to ask about the new dog. “It’s a little yellow puppy,” she said. “It’s very naughty, but it might be better when its tapes have been tied.”

articles.title: BBC removes article linking bare nails trend to ‘white supremacist standards of beauty’
articles.summary: Corporation says story did not meet editorial standards after it attracts criticism from US and UK media. A BBC article that included a claim that a trend for bare nails was linked to “white supremacist standards of beauty” has been permanently removed from its website, after editors concluded it…
body: The article, which first ran on the BBC’s website on 27 September, examined an apparent “viral craze” for bare rather than decorated nails. It said the trend had been flooding social media and fashion catwalks.
It also covered criticisms of the trend, which suggested it could “stigmatise bold manicures”. The article noted that nail art had its roots in black, Latino and Asian communities.

In an early section of the article, it quoted the beauty journalist Kristina Rodulfo as saying: “That trend really promotes blankness and this kind of sameness and erasure of culture and identity that is so important to black and brown communities.
“They are often called elegant or tasteful and these are often usually euphemisms that perpetuate white supremacist standards of beauty.”
points: Corporation says story did not meet editorial standards after it attracts criticism from US and UK media.

articles.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: now is the perfect time to flash some lace
articles.summary: What you need to lift your autumn wardrobe is something flimsy, flirty and unconventional. At this time of year, my job is mostly banging on about jumpers. Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness and merino sweaters, as Keats would surely have written had he been on Substack.
body: I can worship at the altar of cashmere with the best of them. I can extol the virtues of a sweater in tones normally reserved for fine wines and newborn babies. But today I have a rather different proposition for your autumn wardrobe. The best fillip for your shoulder-season style is not a thick layer, but the opposite. What you need to lift your look right now is something flimsy, flirty, with an edging of lace. A sorbet-coloured lace-edged tank top that is virtually a camisole. A slinky black slip skirt with a lace hem. Something with a frill, that has the thrill of lingerie.

Not on its own, obviously, or you will catch your death. You are going to wear your lacy little whatnot and then you are going to partly cover it up by wearing something on top, and this is the whole point.
points: What you need to lift your autumn wardrobe is something flimsy, flirty and unconventional.
At this time of year, my job is mostly banging on about jumpers.
Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness and merino sweaters, as Keats would surely have written had he been on Substack.

articles.title: So long PSL, hello apple-flavored everything – seven snacks we're eyeing this fall
articles.summary: Pumpkin spice is a perennial fall favorite – but apple is the new flavor coming for its crown. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things. Every fall, brands add pumpkin spice to everything, from cereals and sodas to … toilet paper.
body: And the flavor continues to be profitable. In 2025, pumpkin spiced foods garnered an estimated $1.25bn in revenue, according to Future Market Insights.
But this year, another flavor is vying for consumers’ dollars – apple.

In August, McDonald’s released four caramel apple-flavored coffees for the season. That same month, Dairy Queen announced a caramel apple cheesecake Blizzard. The specialty coffee brand La Colombe followed suit, announcing its canned caramel apple draft latte that swiftly sold out – the fastest of any of its releases, according to a brand spokesperson.
Apple-flavored foods have also made their way into grocery aisles, with limited-release launches from popular brands including Olipop (caramel apple), Poppi (sour apple) and RX Bar (apple pie).

articles.title: Toheeb Jimoh Is (Hopefully) Getting Pancakes After the Dior Show
articles.summary: Actor Toheeb Jimoh found time between filming the BBC show ‘Open Water’ and promoting forthcoming films ‘Clarissa’ and ‘Prima Facie’ to head to the Dior show in Paris.
body: “I’m a hoodie guy,” Toheeb Jimoh proclaims. “Day-to-day, you’d catch me in a black tracksuit.”

But when I get chatting with Jimoh immediately after the Dior spring 2027 show, the actor is far from his usual uniform, dressed in an austere navy jacket befitting a Napoleonic ship captain and wide-legged black trousers. Still, he was happy to step out of his comfort zone. “I walked into that room, and the piece just jumped out at me,” Jimoh says of the shearling-lined jacket. “The whole look was just really out there, and it felt great.”

The actor has been plenty busy, between wrapping the BBC show Open Water and promoting forthcoming films Clarissa and Prima Facie. (We’re still waiting to see if Kwabena will crop up in the final season of Industry ). But Jimoh found a bit of time to head to Paris for his second-ever Dior show—his first since Jonathan Anderson took the reins back in April 2025.

articles.title: At the Verity Premiere, Anne Hathaway Reflected on a Five-Film Year—and Her Surprise Baby Joy
articles.summary: "My favorite moment of the year was taking a pregnancy test and finding out it was positive," Anne Hathaway told Vogue on the red carpet. "It was a complete shock! I found out right before everything kicked off.”
body: Five films. Five genres. One very busy year. Anne Hathaway is wrapping up her most ambitious run yet with Verity, the psychological thriller based on Colleen Hoover’s bestselling novel, also starring Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett.

On Tuesday evening, the trio joined Hoover for the film’s premiere at New York’s AMC Lincoln Square, just days before Verity hits theaters on October 2. Hathaway arrived in a custom Prabal Gurung gown, capping off a whirlwind season marked by a packed slate of projects, press tours, and public appearances. Was she starting to lose count?

“No, no, no! Five is a lot, but I haven’t lost track because I’ve had so much help,” Hathaway told Vogue with a laugh. “Everything has not been effortless with all the back-to-back press and red carpets. There’s been an army of people behind me at every step, and I’m just really lucky. This year has all been really amazing. For most actors, we are lucky to get one film a year, but to have a year that’s been ridiculously overly-blessed, I’m appreciating every second of it.”
points: "My favorite moment of the year was taking a pregnancy test and finding out it was positive," Anne Hathaway told Vogue on the red carpet.
I found out right before everything kicked off.”

articles.title: Exclusive: Sophia Bush and Ashlyn Harris Are Married! The Romantic Story Behind Their Special Day
articles.summary: Bush and Harris tied the knot in a private ceremony in an upstate New York backyard—and the pared-down wedding turned out to fit the happy couple perfectly.
body: Actor and debut author Sophia Bush’s new memoir, And I Will Tell You Mine: Notes from a Life in Progress, includes plenty of revelations—but perhaps the most exciting among them? The news that she and her partner of three years, former professional soccer player Ashlyn Harris, are now wife and wife.
Bush and Harris tied the knot in a private ceremony in upstate New York in the summer of 2025, with Harris’s children, Sloane and Ocean (to whom Bush is a proud stepmother), in attendance.

The event’s intimate scale suited the happy couple perfectly. “When you get to this stage in your life, you begin to unpack what’s yours and what’s always sort of been for everyone else,” Bush tells Vogue via Zoom, with Harris seated by her side. She adds, addressing her wife: “You’ve been playing in stadiums in front of 60,000 people since you were 15 or 16, and I started playing a character for tens of millions of people when I was 21. It’s such a privilege to be able to perform as an athlete or an actor, but it also comes with certain costs.”
points: Bush and Harris tied the knot in a private ceremony in an upstate New York backyard—and the pared-down wedding turned out to fit the happy couple perfectly.

articles.title: Your Mac Should Be Doing More of the Work. Here's How MacPaw Helps
articles.summary: The work you actually sat down to do rarely gets interrupted by something dramatic. It gets interrupted by housekeeping—a quick fix here, a quick lookup there, each one small enough to feel harmless and just long enough to break your focus.
body: This is true for freelancers, founders, designers, and developers. But it’s also true for work-from-home employees and busy people in general. And it’s not that any of these tasks are difficult (which almost makes them more annoying); it’s that each one takes just enough time and attention to pull you away from whatever you actually sat down to do. Little interruptions may not seem like much, but they add up to a surprising amount of time spent taking care of your Mac instead of letting your Mac take care of you.

MacPaw has spent 18 years building tools that take everyday work off Mac users' hands by noticing the small stuff you've stopped noticing, and quietly handling it for you. For anyone whose Mac doubles as an office, the files, apps, and projects add up—but the upkeep shouldn't have to.
Here’s how MacPaw’s products help you save time and frustration while using your trusty Mac computer.

When storage starts disappearing, you can open folders one by one, sort through old downloads, track down duplicate files, and try to uncover large files that are eating up space and collecting dust. Or, you can make that maintenance somebody else's problem.

articles.title: I Tried 7 Loaves from This New Bread Subscription Service, and They Taste Just as Good as Homemade
articles.summary: There’s truly nothing like a good, freshly baked loaf of sourdough to me. And as much as I enjoy baking sourdough myself, tending to a starter can get tedious. When I moved recently I had to say goodbye to my starter, and now if I want sourdough I need to buy it. That’s where Bittman’s comes in.
body: The folks behind Bittman’s are father-daughter team Mark and Kate Bittman. Mark is a New York Times -bestselling author, notable for his How to Cook Everything books, and Kate has a background in PR. Together, the two host the podcast Food with Mark Bittman, work on The Bittman Project, and run Bittman’s, their frozen sourdough delivery service.

There are nine sourdoughs to choose from: Corn, Cinnamon Walnut Raisin, Whole Wheat, Half Wheat, Rye, Focaccia, Ciabatta Flats, and Demi Baguettes. The brand also offers croissants (which at the time of writing were sold out), as well as accoutrements like butter, olive oil, and chocolate hazelnut spread.

I’ve received two shipments of Bittman’s sourdough and have tried all of the breads, except the Whole Wheat loaf and the Ciabatta Flats. The one I was most intrigued by is the Corn Sourdough. It has sweetness from the corn, but with that chewy-on-the-inside texture I love about sourdough. I enjoyed it with strawberry jam or butter and a sprinkling of flaky salt. This is such a unique offering, and I’ve enjoyed it both times I’ve had it.
